artists.biography: James is a British rock band from Manchester, England. They formed in 1982 and were active throughout the 1980s, but most successful during the 1990s. Their hit singles include "Come Home", "Sit Down", and "She's a Star" as well as their American college radio hit "Laid". Following the departure of lead singer Tim Booth in 2001, the band became inactive but re-formed in January 2007, returning for a new album and international tour. Up to 2010, the band had sold more than 25 million albums worldwide.

Their hit singles include "Come Home", "Sit Down", and "She's a Star" as well as their American college radio hit "Laid". Up to 2010, the band had sold more than 25 million albums worldwide.

release_name_discogs: Be Opened By The Wonderful (40 Years Orchestrated)

perplexity.description:
Be Opened By The Wonderful (40 Years Orchestrated), released in 2023, is a double album by British band James that reimagines their career-spanning hits and fan favorites through orchestral arrangements. The album features 20 tracks (19 on vinyl) that span from early songs like "Why So Close" (1986) to selections from their critically acclaimed 2021 album All The Colours Of You. Orchestrated and conducted by Joe Duddell with the ORCA22 Orchestra and the Manchester Inspirational Voices choir, the album blends the band's rock roots with classical instrumentation, creating a lush, acoustic soundscape that highlights the emotional depth of their songwriting.

This release marks a significant milestone in James’s discography, celebrating their 40th anniversary by revisiting and transforming their music with orchestral grandeur. It follows their 2021 studio album All The Colours Of You and precedes their 2024 album Yummy. The project was recorded at Blueprint Studios in Manchester and showcases reworked versions of iconic tracks such as "Sit Down," "Laid," and "She’s A Star," emphasizing the band’s evolution and versatility over four decades.

Critically, Be Opened By The Wonderful was well received for its ambitious orchestral reinterpretations, with praise for the arrangements and the band’s ability to breathe new life into their catalog. Commercially, the album reached No. 3 on the UK charts, reflecting both fan enthusiasm and critical acclaim. The release was supported by a UK tour featuring live orchestral performances, underscoring the album’s unique fusion of rock and classical elements and its celebratory nature within James’s extensive body of work.
